headline: Revenue growth accelerates, margins expand broadly
summary_short: TI's Q2 FY2026 revenue rose 22.8% y/y to $5,463M and diluted EPS grew 51.8% to $2.14, as GAAP operating margin expanded to 42.3% from 35.1% a year ago.
summary_long: Revenue grew 22.8% y/y to $5,463M and 13.2% q/q, led by Analog (+26% y/y) and Embedded Processing (+16% y/y); the smaller Other segment declined 2%. Operating margin expanded to 42.3% from 35.1% a year ago as revenue growth outpaced a smaller rise in R&D/SG&A. Diluted EPS rose 51.8% y/y to $2.14, including a 5-cent benefit not in TI's original guidance. Trailing-12-month free cash flow more than tripled to $6,534M (33.6% of revenue) from $1,763M (10.6%), helped by $1,179M of CHIPS Act incentive proceeds. Cash plus short-term investments rose to $7,001M from $5,103M q/q. TI guides Q3 2026 revenue to $5.65B-$6.15B and EPS to $2.23-$2.57.

drivers.explanation: CEO cites broad-based growth led by industrial, data center and automotive; by segment, Analog revenue grew 26% y/y and Embedded Processing grew 16% y/y, while the smaller Other segment declined 2%.
Operating margin expanded roughly 720bp y/y to 42.3% from 35.1% as revenue grew 22.8% while cost of revenue, R&D and SG&A together grew far more slowly.
EPS included a 5-cent benefit that was not in the company's original guidance, per the release.
CEO Haviv Ilan cites strength of the business model and 300mm production; over the trailing 12 months TI invested $3.9B in R&D and SG&A, $3.3B in capex, and returned $5.8B to owners.
Trailing-12-month free cash flow more than tripled to $6,534M (33.6% of revenue) from $1,763M (10.6%), partly aided by $1,179M of CHIPS Act incentive proceeds versus $260M a year earlier.
